What is the primary definition of astrology in this introductory context?
column2: It is the study of the motions of planets through our solar system and how those energies affect our physical lives.

column1: What term is used for planets in Vedic astrology, and what is its literal translation?
column2: Grahas, which translates to "seizers" (as they seize our consciousness and push us in certain directions).

column1: According to the Vedic perspective, what does a person's birth chart fundamentally reflect?
column2: It is a snapshot of our past habits, tendencies, choices, and desires from previous lifetimes.

column1: Are the planets viewed as purely external forces in Vedic astrology?
column2: No, they are considered gateways or transmitters of karma, functioning as aspects of our own consciousness.

column1: What is the primary reason the speaker advises against general mundane (worldly) astrology predictions?
column2: Because external events (like transits) will generally only affect an individual if they already possess a matching tendency or predisposition in their own birth chart (inner cosmos).

column1: In the speaker's car analogy, what does the momentum of a fast-moving car represent?
column2: Our past karma and ingrained habits.

column1: In the car analogy for karma, what does applying the brakes represent?
column2: Remedial measures that actively slow down or exhaust past karmic momentum.

column1: What current historical age (Yuga) does the speaker state we are currently beginning?
column2: The Dwapara Yuga.

column1: Why is meditation or yoga highly recommended alongside the study of Vedic astrology?
column2: It brings conscious awareness to our inner energies, providing the detachment needed to consciously choose whether to engage with ingrained karmic patterns.

column1: According to the concept of the inner and outer cosmos, how are planetary influences primarily experienced?
column2: They affect us internally, causing us to experience situations that only seemingly occur externally.

column1: What does the term Veda essentially mean in the context of Vedic science?
column2: It means knowledge, specifically self-revealed knowledge that comes from direct experience rather than just books.

column1: According to the transcript, what are the four main areas of life (aims) that the houses in astrology deal with?
column2:
• Dharma (inspiration/purpose)
  • Artha (developing resources)
  • Kama (exploring desire and pleasure)
  • Moksha (liberation/meditation)

column1: Is the planet Jupiter universally helpful for all ascendants in Vedic astrology?
column2: No. While it is a great benefic, it can hinder the dharma and purpose for certain ascendants like Virgo or Gemini, but is very helpful for Aries, Cancer, or Leo.

column1: What do the nodes Rahu and Ketu represent in terms of our incarnated consciousness?
column2:
They represent our karmic path:
  • Ketu shows where we have been in past lifetimes (existing skills/talents).
  • Rahu shows what we are aiming to develop in this lifetime (unfamiliar goals and desires).

column1: Why does the speaker advise against seeking ultimate fulfillment through the placement of Ketu?
column2: Because Ketu represents past attachments and obsessions we must let go of. True growth requires focusing on perfecting the unexplored desires of Rahu.

column1: How should a conscious individual respond to the urge to act out negative Karma?
column2: By developing detachment. Instead of using karma as an excuse for bad behavior, one should consciously pause and choose not to perpetuate the cycle of karma.

column1: What happens to our relationship with the planets as we advance in self-realization?
column2: We stop seeing them as external forces ("seizers") that push us around, and begin to recognize them as essential aspects of ourselves that must be integrated in harmony.

column1: Why does the speaker say we should focus on satvic behaviors (kindness, benevolence) if it won't permanently change the world?
column2: Because choosing peace and clarity lifts our own consciousness, eventually liberating us from needing to incarnate in this particular worldly testing ground again.

column1: According to the transcript, are the roles indicated by our birth chart strictly limited to specific careers?
column2: No. Career is just one aspect. Our role might be simply acting a certain way towards someone to help them fulfill their karma, fitting into the larger design of infinite Consciousness.

column1: What is one of the main problems with how people approach astrology?
column2: They become fatalistic, believing the chart's indications are completely fixed and unavoidable.

column1: How should astrological indications be viewed instead of as fixed events?
column2: As trends, possibilities, or weather patterns.

column1: When does the promise of a birth chart operate as absolute fate?
column2: When a person remains unconscious and acts purely on past habits and conditioning.

column1: What does the birth chart represent in the context of fate vs. free will?
column2: The static promise of what is possible from the moment of birth.

column1: When does free will actively occur?
column2: When you consciously decide to shift your attention and actions in a new direction, rather than reacting to past patterns.

column1: What are five methods mentioned for changing your fate and exercising free will?
column2:
• Gemstones
  • Mantras
  • Behavior modification
  • Yoga
  • Service

column1: Why is service considered one of the best remedies for overcoming personal difficulties?
column2: It takes your mind off your own problems while supporting another person's consciousness.

column1: How does a strong negative karma respond to free will and action?
column2: Conscious actions change the odds in your favor by shifting momentum, even if the initial karma is intense.

column1: What is the core danger of constantly relying on astrology to predict the future?
column2: It prevents you from learning, growing, and consciously making choices to overcome challenges.

column1: According to the transcript, what are the three main roles of an astrologer?
column2:
• To be an objective witness to a person's Karma (analyzing and acknowledging strengths/weaknesses).
  • To bring hidden or unconscious aspects of a person's life to light.
  • To show a path of success towards a goal that fulfills their life path.

column1: According to the transcript, do worldly success and happiness always go together?
column2: No. Many successful people are miserable inside, while some who achieve little feel their lives have great purpose.

column1: What should an astrologer do if a client has severe psychological unhappiness they do not know how to address?
column2: Refer the client to a professional, such as a psychologist, psychiatrist, or healer.

column1: In this transcript, which zodiac sign is associated with coming to terms with our psychological problems?
column2: Aquarius.

column1: In this transcript, which zodiac sign is considered the sign of Liberation (freedom from the cycle of birth and death)?
column2: Pisces.

column1: According to the Bhagavad Gita principle mentioned, to what is a person entitled regarding their actions?
column2: They are entitled to the action only, not to the fruits (results) of their actions.

column1: Why is it important for an astrologer to avoid making judgmental predictions about success or failure?
column2: Because success or failure is no indication of inner peace or inspiration; both are simply parts of everyone's path.

column1: What should an astrologer do if they cannot see the answer to a client's question in the chart?
column2: Be completely honest and say, "I don't see that in the chart." Do not try to be a know-it-all or impress people.

column1: According to an experienced Indian astrologer referenced in the lecture, what is the most essential daily practice to become a good astrologer?
column2: "Always tell the truth" in daily life. This develops an inner sense of truth that helps you intuitively know when a chart interpretation feels correct.

column1: Should an astrologer expect to give 100% accurate advice all the time?
column2: No. Astrology deals with trends and possibilities. The world isn't about absolute certainty, so expecting 100% accuracy is unrealistic.

column1: What is the primary benefit of meditation and spiritual practice for an individual according to Vedic astrology?
column2: It creates distance and detachment from blind identification with habits, thoughts, and transient experiences, reducing suffering.

column1: How does meditation specifically help a practicing astrologer?
column2:
• Increases objectivity and clarity.
  • Organizes the mind to better synthesize complex chart components.
  • Prevents the astrologer's own personality and preferences from coloring the reading.

column1: Which specific house and planet are associated with the broad-mindedness, discernment, and clarity needed to be a good astrologer?
column2: A well-supported 5th house / 5th house lord, and the planet Jupiter.

column1: Which planetary placements are mentioned as potentially making a person selfish in relationships?
column2: A strong or well-dignified Venus and Moon in the 7th house, 3rd house, or any relationship-related house.

column1: Which planetary influences on the Ascendant can cause frustration and overly high expectations in relationships?
column2: Mars and Saturn located on, aspecting, or impacting the Ascendant or Ascendant lord.

column1: What two ways must different karmas be handled when they manifest in life?
column2:
• Reversible karmas: Can be altered through corrective action (e.g., diet or exercise).
  • Irreversible karmas: Cannot be undone once started and must simply be waited out (e.g., a poison ivy rash).

column1: What analogy does the speaker use to describe our blind identification with our birth chart?
column2: Being engrossed in reading a book—we become so fixated on the specific story that we forget our broader environment and the ability to make other choices.

column1: According to the transcript, why is the concept of detachment in the Yoga Sutras essential for working with astrology?
column2: It frees us from fixation on our specific personality and astrological influences, giving us the latitude to make new choices and experience the totality of our being.

column1: What is the proper role of an astrologer when counseling a client?
column2: To see what is there as clearly as possible and share it with integrity, rather than telling the client what to do or being attached to the results.

column1: What should an astrologer do if a client immediately rejects true and objective astrological advice?
column2: Practice detachment and let it go; share the information without forcing it, as the client may need months or years to recognize its truth.

column1: What specific meditation technique does the speaker recommend for astrologers to clear their mind and release attachments?
column2: Chakra meditation (specifically Kriya Yoga), which involves circulating life force and awareness through the chakras and spine.

column1: What do the Planets represent in Vedic Astrology?
column2: They represent the conscious forces within the chart (the "beings" that give animation or life). On a microcosmic level, they represent specific aspects of our own consciousness.

column1: What does the Sun represent?
column2:
• Inner Light/Spirit, the ego (projecting onto the world), and inner state of clarity
  • Authority figures, royalty, government, and the father
  • Vitality, solid body, bones, and consistency
  • Ability to do our duty

column1: What does the Moon represent?
column2:
• The mother and formative early environment
  • Our adaptability, intuition, empathy, and how we connect with others
  • Popularity, caring for people, the general public, and females
  • Fertility and the body's blood/fluids

column1: What does Mercury represent?
column2:
• The rational/logical mind, planning, and ability to manage the affairs of life
  • Communication (thought/speech/writing), acting, and skills
  • Trade, business, and short distance travels
  • Youthfulness, the skin, and nervous system

column1: What does Mars represent?
column2:
• Energy, drive, courage, instinct, and passion
  • Knowing which battles are worth fighting (taking proper initiative)
  • Capacity to use logic and reason
  • Technical skills, sports, weapons, and younger siblings
  • Physical strength, muscles, and surgery/accidents

column1: What does Jupiter represent?
column2:
• Innate wisdom, higher knowledge, and teaching/counseling
  • Seeing the bigger picture with optimism, faith, and luck
  • Spirituality, religion, the Guru, forgiveness, and grace
  • Children, elder brothers, and body fat

column1: What does Venus represent?
column2:
• Love, romance, marriage, and harmony
  • Comfort, arts, beauty, luxuries, and making choices for long-term fulfillment
  • Managing anger (cooling us down)
  • Sensuality, fertility, reproductive fluids, and ability to rejuvenate/regenerate the body (endurance)

column1: What does Saturn represent?
column2:
• Capacity to endure, face the hard road, patience, and practicality
  • Restriction, limitation, and accepting liabilities/weaknesses
  • Negative aspects: sorrow, despondency, poverty, hard work
  • Detachment and spiritual growth through renunciation
  • Time, longevity, old age, nerves, and the immune system

column1: What are Rahu and Ketu, and how do they function?
column2: They are shadow planets (points in space where eclipses occur) that give results in relation to their Lords. They show where our inner light becomes eclipsed by attachments, aversions, obsessions, or compulsions.

column1: What is the specific focus of Ketu vs. Rahu?
column2:
• Ketu (South Node): Inward/introvert energy. Gives obsessions, represents past skills to balance. Associated with sudden losses/viruses, and is the ultimate bestower of spiritual liberation (Moksha).
  • Rahu (North Node): Outward/extrovert energy. Gives compulsions and intense worldly desires/ambitions. Represents illusion, manipulation, and what we lack success in/are meant to develop in this lifetime.

column1: What do the Houses represent generally?
column2: They represent the different areas of life.

column1: What does the 1st House represent?
column2:
• The physical body (especially the head), vitality, and general health
  • Personality, self-awareness, and self-projection (how other people see us)
  • General disposition and start in life

column1: What does the 2nd House represent?
column2:
• Wealth, finances, resources, and personal values/responsibilities
  • Speech (truthfulness) and the face/mouth
  • Food we eat and early childhood experiences

column1: What does the 3rd House represent?
column2:
• Younger siblings and peers
  • Courage, initiative, and success through one's own efforts
  • Communication, hobbies, fine arts, and mental curiosity/skills
  • How we logically think about things

column1: What does the 4th House represent?
column2:
• The mother
  • Home, property, and vehicles
  • Our inner emotional state, psychological well-being, and the heart

column1: What does the 5th House represent?
column2:
• Children and romantic pleasures/love affairs
  • Creativity, intelligence, and spiritual practices (mantras)
  • Speculative investments
  • Good past life Karma

column1: What does the 6th House represent?
column2:
• Health and disease
  • Enemies, competitors, and debts we must overcome
  • Daily jobs, routines, and service to others

column1: What does the 7th House represent?
column2:
• Spouse and long-term partnerships
  • How we relate to 'other people' (including open enemies)
  • Business, commerce, trade, and things vanishing from sight
  • Foreign travel and lands

column1: What does the 8th House represent?
column2:
• Length of life, death, and chronic illness
  • Hidden aspects of life, inner psychological stability, and how we deal with crisis/sudden breaks
  • Conjugal bond, sexual intimacy, and hidden resources (joint finances/partner's money)
  • Occult and psychic strength

column1: What does the 9th House represent?
column2:
• Morals, Dharma, religion, philosophy, and purpose in life
  • The father, Gurus, and higher education
  • Luck, fortune, grace, and long journeys
  • Marriage and committed relationships

column1: What does the 10th House represent?
column2:
• Career, achievements, and capacity to be active (life purpose in the world)
  • Status, fame, prestige, and honour
  • Authority figures and government
  • Good deeds that benefit society

column1: What does the 11th House represent?
column2:
• Major goals, ambitions, and desires
  • Larger social circles, organizations, older friends, and elder siblings
  • Gains, profits, titles, awards, and supplemental income

column1: What does the 12th House represent?
column2:
• Hidden areas like loss and expenses
  • The subconscious (sleep, dreams, the bedroom) and states of consciousness
  • Isolated institutions (hospitals, prisons) and distant lands
  • Contemplation, meditation, secluded spiritual practices, and spiritual liberation (Moksha) / after-death states

column1: What do the Signs (Rasis) represent in Vedic Astrology?
column2: They are the fields of energy patterns that act as a backdrop, showing how the planets are going to work within the houses.

column1: In terms of active and passive signs, how are the odd-numbered signs classified?
column2: As Active signs

column1: In terms of active and passive signs, how are the even-numbered signs classified?
column2: As Passive signs

column1: What are the three qualities (modalities) of signs in their repeating order?
column2:
• Active
  • Fixed
  • Dual

column1: What is the primary behavioral trait of an Active sign?
column2: They take initiative and indicate change.

column1: What is the primary behavioral trait of a Fixed sign?
column2: Preserving things, maintaining the status quo, and holding things together.

column1: How do the first and last 15 degrees of a Dual sign behave?
column2:
• First 15 degrees: Acts like a Fixed sign
  • Last 15 degrees: Acts like an Active sign

column1: What is the repeating order of the four elements through the zodiac signs?
column2: Fire, Earth, Air, Water

column1: Which three signs belong to the Fire element?
column2:
• Aries
  • Leo
  • Sagittarius

column1: Which three signs belong to the Earth element?
column2:
• Taurus
  • Virgo
  • Capricorn

column1: Which three signs belong to the Air element?
column2:
• Gemini
  • Libra
  • Aquarius

column1: Which three signs belong to the Water element?
column2:
• Cancer
  • Scorpio
  • Pisces

column1: Which astrological element is associated with the Brahmin class (scholars and teachers)?
column2: Water signs

column1: Which astrological element is associated with the Kshatriya class (warriors and defenders)?
column2: Fire signs

column1: Which astrological element is associated with the Vaishya class (merchants and commerce)?
column2: Air signs

column1: Which astrological element is associated with the Shudra class (servants and workers)?
column2: Earth signs

column1: In Vedic astrology, if the Ascendant falls at a late degree (e.g., 29 degrees) of a sign, what portion of that sign becomes the first house?
column2: The whole sign becomes the first house, regardless of the degree.

column1: Which houses make up the Angles, and where are they visually located in a North Indian chart?
column2:
• Houses: 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th
  • Location: The four diamonds right in the middle of the chart.

column1: What do the Angles (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th houses) represent in a person's life?
column2: They represent the more active and obvious aspects or main activities of life.

column1: Which houses make up the Trines?
column2: The 1st, 5th, and 9th houses.

column1: What role do the Trines (1st, 5th, 9th houses) play in a person's life?
column2: They act as supports for the main activities of our life.

column1: Which houses are considered more "hidden" or less immediately obvious in a chart?
column2: The 2nd, 3rd, 6th, 8th, 11th, and 12th houses.

column1: What are the three self factors to analyze to find the foundational baseline of a chart?
column2:
To determine the baseline foundation, analyze:
  • The Sun
  • The Ascendant Lord
  • The Atmakaraka

column1: How does a strong or well-supported Sun manifest in a person's life?
column2:
A strong Sun indicates a person who is:
  • Confident
  • Knows what they are here to do
  • Has the inner inspiration to follow their path

column1: What happens when the Sun is debilitated or poorly placed?
column2: The capacity to live out one's inspiration is frustrated, weaker, or held back.

column1: Which houses are generally considered good placements for the Moon to feel content?
column2:
The Moon is more comfortable in the:
  • 4th House (especially good for peace and harmony)
  • 9th House
  • 10th House

column1: What are the traditional aspects of a planet on the Moon?
column2: Traditional aspects occur when any planet is in the 7th house from the Moon (directly across).

column1: What are the specific additional aspects for Mars?
column2: Mars aspects planets that are 4, 7, and 8 houses away from it.

column1: What are the specific additional aspects for Saturn?
column2: Saturn aspects planets that are 3, 7, and 10 houses away from it.

column1: What are the specific additional aspects for Jupiter?
column2: Jupiter aspects planets that are 5, 7, and 9 houses away from it.

column1: How do benefic aspects (e.g., Jupiter, Venus, Mercury) affect the Moon?
column2: They make a person more comfortable with the ease and enjoyable aspects of life, finding contentment in flow and beauty.

column1: What does a Jupiter aspect on the Moon indicate about a person's emotional nature?
column2: The person is comfortable with joy, grace, optimism, and a sense of bigger purpose or knowledge.

column1: How do malefic aspects (e.g., Saturn, Mars, Sun, Rahu, Ketu) affect the Moon?
column2: They make a person more comfortable with difficulty, change, or adventure, and they may feel uneasy when things go perfectly smoothly.

column1: What is the emotional nature of someone with Mars aspecting the Moon?
column2: They have an aggressive or active emotional nature, needing stimulation, action, adventure, and initiative.

column1: How does a Saturn aspect on the Moon manifest in a person's life?
column2: It makes a person used to sorrow, suffering, and hardship, often indicating early life struggles or leading to careers that deal with helping others in difficulty.

column1: What is Kuja Dosha, and why can it be beneficial if both partners have it?
column2: Kuja Dosha relates to a strong Mars influence. If both partners have it, they understand each other's need for excitement, change, and taking initiative.

column1: What does it mean when the Sun or Moon is in an angular house (1, 4, 7, 10)?
column2: The person will take more action and initiative towards the qualities of that planet.

column1: What is the effect of placing the Sun or Moon in a trinal house?
column2: The planet's significations work with more grace and ease.

column1: What do the 6th, 8th, and 12th houses indicate for the Sun or Moon?
column2:
• 6th House: Delays and debts
  • 8th House: Sudden breaks, changes, or innate weaknesses
  • 12th House: Loss, sacrifice, or expenses to be paid off

column1: What is the difference between the Sun and the Moon regarding the Soul?
column2: The Sun represents the absolute Soul before embodiment (pure impulse), while the Moon represents the embodied soul (individualized history, tendencies, and emotions).

column1: How often do the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant change signs?
column2:
• Sun: Every 30 days
  • Moon: Every ~2.25 days
  • Ascendant: Every 2 hours

column1: What is the order of importance when looking at the specifics of a chart?
column2:
1. Ascendant (most specific)
  2. Moon
  3. Sun (least specific)

column1: How do benefic planets generally deliver their results?
column2: They are gentle and kind, bringing results easily and naturally without requiring hard work.

column1: How do malefic planets generally deliver their results?
column2: They bring stress and strain, requiring you to work hard and earn your results.

column1: What positive, necessary role does Saturn play despite being a malefic?
column2: He gives the capacity to endure, handle difficult situations, do tedious work, and ultimately achieve success.

column1: How does Saturn behave when in a weak state (bad dignity)?
column2: Causes laziness, lack of endurance, and giving up easily when hardships arise.

column1: How can a benefic like Jupiter cause problems when in bad dignity?
column2: Can cause one to trust luck too much, expect things to come too easily, and misjudge opportunities.

column1: For an Aries ascendant, which planets are considered friendly (functional benefics)?
column2:
• Sun (rules 5th)
  • Moon (rules 4th)
  • Mars (rules 1st)
  • Jupiter (rules 9th)

column1: Which house lords generally get in the way of success or are considered functional malefics?
column2: Lords of the 3rd, 6th, and 11th houses, as well as Maraka (killer) houses like the 2nd and 7th.

column1: Why is the Sun considered a difficult planet for a Libra ascendant?
column2: Because it rules the 11th house, which is considered a primary obstacle builder and Raja Yoga breaker.

column1: What does Shadbala literally mean in Vedic Astrology?
column2: Six strengths (Shad = six, Bala = strength)

column1: In Shadbala scoring, what value indicates a planet is considered strong?
column2: A score above 1.0

column1: What is Uchchabala based on?
column2: A planet's placement relative to its exaltation position (closer to exaltation = stronger)

column1: What is Chestabala based on?
column2: A planet's retrograde status and its closeness to Earth

column1: What does Kendrabala measure and what does it provide a planet?
column2: It measures placement in an angle (houses 1, 4, 7, 10). It gives the capacity to take initiative and accomplish goals

column1: What is Digbala?
column2: Directional strength (a planet's strength based on its location in a specific house or part of the sky)

column1: How are a planet's Ishta (capacity for good) and Kashta (capacity for ill) mathematically derived?
column2: By adding Uchchabala and Chestabala, then dividing by two

column1: Does a retrograde status mathematically "cancel" a planet's debilitation?
column2: No. The debilitated planet still has 0 Uchchabala, but gains high Chestabala (from being retrograde), giving it an average Ishta rather than true cancellation

column1: What is the ultimate purpose of Jyotish (Vedic Astrology)?
column2: To promote Self-realization, reveal reality as it is, and liberate the soul from suffering.

column1: According to Patanjali's Yoga Sutra II.16, what type of pain is to be avoided?
column2: Pain which has not yet manifested.

column1: What secondary supports/remedies are prescribed in Vedic Astrology to balance planetary energies?
column2: Faultless gemstones, planetary mantras, color therapy, aromatherapy, and precious metals.

column1: Why is the Moon given more interpretive weight in Jyotish than in Western astrology?
column2: We cannot look directly at the Sun, but we can gaze at the Moon's reflection. The Moon makes the Sun's spiritual light manageable for physical incarnation.

column1: What do the Sun and Moon signify regarding parentage?
column2: Sun signifies the father (authority figure). Moon signifies the mother (formative emotional nurturer).

column1: What physical body parts and tissues do the Sun and Moon represent?
column2:
Sun: The bones and heart (vitality).
Moon: The blood and bodily fluids (circulatory environment).

column1: Why are both the Moon and Mercury afflicted in cases of severe mental illness?
column2: The Moon rules sensory perception, while Mercury rules cognitive integration. When both fail, the mind cannot process environmental inputs.

column1: What physical tissues are ruled by Mercury?
column2: The skin (and coverings of anything, including cell membranes) and blood vessels (circulatory containers).

column1: What are the primary worldly and physical significations of Mars?
column2: Younger siblings, physical strength/muscle tissue, technical/engineering skills, weapons, fire, metals, and surgery.

column1: What physical organs and tissues does Jupiter relate to in Ayur-astrology?
column2: The brain, liver, and adipose (fat) tissue.

column1: Esoterically, why is Jupiter the primary indicator for a student of astrology or counseling?
column2: Jupiter rules the ether element and the power of 'hearing' higher, philosophical wisdom and counsel.

column1: What are the key physiological significations of Venus?
column2: Muscle tissue, DNA strength, reproductive fluids (semen), and the digestive tract's ability to absorb nutrients.

column1: Why is a prominent Saturn key to genuine spiritual evolution?
column2: It provides true detachment and renunciation (peace with reality) rather than spiritual escapism.

column1: What is the core spiritual advice for managing the house containing Ketu?
column2: Treat that area with unconditional love and absolute surrender (as service to the Divine), without seeking personal ego-gratification.

column1: What is the difference between Saturn's fears and Rahu's fears?
column2: Saturn's fears are realistic, based on past experience of suffering. Rahu's fears are phobias and unfounded anxieties about the unknown.

column1: What are the rules of dignity (Exaltation, Moolatrikona, Fall, and Swakshetra) and their exact degrees for the Sun?
column2:
Rules: Leo
Exalted: Aries (greatest at 10° Aries)
Moolatrikona: Leo (0° to 20° Leo)
Own Sign (Swakshetra): Leo (20° to 30° Leo)
Fall: Libra (deepest at 10° Libra)

column1: What are the rules of dignity (Exaltation, Moolatrikona, Fall, and Swakshetra) and their exact degrees for the Moon?
column2:
Rules: Cancer
Exalted: Taurus (0° to 3° Taurus, greatest at 3° Taurus)
Moolatrikona: Taurus (3° to 30° Taurus)
Own Sign (Swakshetra): Cancer (3° to 30° Cancer)
Fall: Scorpio (deepest at 3° Scorpio)

column1: What are the rules of dignity (Exaltation, Moolatrikona, Fall, and Swakshetra) and their exact degrees for Mars?
column2:
Rules: Aries & Scorpio
Exalted: Capricorn (greatest at 28° Capricorn)
Moolatrikona: Aries (0° to 12° Aries)
Own Sign (Swakshetra): Aries (20° to 30° Aries) and all of Scorpio
Fall: Cancer (deepest at 28° Cancer)

column1: What are the rules of dignity (Exaltation, Moolatrikona, Fall, and Swakshetra) and their exact degrees for Mercury?
column2:
Rules: Gemini & Virgo
Exalted: Virgo (0° to 15° Virgo, greatest at 15° Virgo)
Moolatrikona: Virgo (15° to 20° Virgo)
Own Sign (Swakshetra): All of Gemini and Virgo (20° to 30° Virgo)
Fall: Pisces (deepest at 15° Pisces)

column1: What are the rules of dignity (Exaltation, Moolatrikona, Fall, and Swakshetra) and their exact degrees for Jupiter?
column2:
Rules: Sagittarius & Pisces
Exalted: Cancer (greatest at 5° Cancer)
Moolatrikona: Sagittarius (0° to 5° Sagittarius)
Own Sign (Swakshetra): Sagittarius (5° to 30° Sagittarius) and all of Pisces
Fall: Capricorn (deepest at 5° Capricorn)

column1: What are the rules of dignity (Exaltation, Moolatrikona, Fall, and Swakshetra) and their exact degrees for Venus?
column2:
Rules: Taurus & Libra
Exalted: Pisces (greatest at 27° Pisces)
Moolatrikona: Libra (0° to 20° Libra)
Own Sign (Swakshetra): All of Taurus and Libra (20° to 30° Libra)
Fall: Virgo (deepest at 27° Virgo)

column1: What are the rules of dignity (Exaltation, Moolatrikona, Fall, and Swakshetra) and their exact degrees for Saturn?
column2:
Rules: Capricorn & Aquarius
Exalted: Libra (greatest at 20° Libra)
Moolatrikona: Aquarius (0° to 20° Aquarius)
Own Sign (Swakshetra): All of Capricorn and Aquarius (20° to 30° Aquarius)
Fall: Aries (deepest at 20° Aries)

column1: What are the different classical opinions on the Exaltation, Own Sign, and Fall of the Lunar Nodes (Rahu and Ketu)?
column2:
Many classical texts disagree, but two main views prevail:
1. Ramadayalu / Sanketanidhi: Rahu is exalted in Gemini, rules Virgo; Ketu is exalted in Sagittarius, rules Pisces.
2. Most classical authors (e.g. Parasara): Rahu is exalted in Taurus (compatible with Venus/Saturn), Ketu is exalted in Scorpio (compatible with Mars/Jupiter). Both do well in Gemini and Virgo.

column1: According to the percentage-based system of planetary strength due to sign placement, what are the strengths of a planet from its fall to its exaltation?
column2:
- Fall (Debilitation): up to 12.5% strength
- Enemy sign: up to 25%
- Neutral sign: up to 37.5%
- Friend's sign: up to 50%
- Own negative sign: up to 62.5%
- Own positive sign: up to 75%
- Moolatrikona: up to 87.5%
- Exalted: up to 100% strength

column1: What is the Sanskrit term for a planetary aspect, and what does it represent esoterically?
column2: Drishti (glance). It represents the ability of a planet to project its conscious energy to other signs/houses of the zodiac other than the one it resides in.

column1: What is the baseline planetary aspect (Drishti) that all planets share, and what is its strength?
column2: The 7th house aspect. All planets cast a full-strength (100% or full sight) aspect on the sign/house directly opposite (180° away) from their position.

column1: What are the classical 'finer aspects' (partial strengths/sights) for the 3rd and 10th houses from any planet?
column2: All planets cast quarter-strength (25%) sight on the 3rd and 10th houses, except Saturn which casts 100% full sight on them.

column1: What are the classical 'finer aspects' (partial strengths/sights) for the 5th and 9th houses from any planet?
column2: All planets cast half-strength (50%) sight on the 5th and 9th houses, except Jupiter which casts 100% full sight on them.

column1: What are the classical 'finer aspects' (partial strengths/sights) for the 4th and 8th houses from any planet?
column2: All planets cast three-quarter-strength (75%) sight on the 4th and 8th houses, except Mars which casts 100% full sight on them.

column1: What is the Sanskrit term for a shared connection or mutual relationship between two planets (such as exchanging signs or mutually aspecting each other)?
column2: Sambhanda. This occurs when planets exchange signs (mutual reception), conjoin in the same sign, or mutually aspect each other.

column1: What are the four sensitive pillars of a house's strength?
column2:
1. Planets residing in the house.
2. Planets aspecting the house.
3. The placement/condition of the house lord.
4. The natural significator (Karaka) for that house.

column1: Which planets are considered general benefics and standard malefics in Vedic astrology?
column2:
Benefics: Jupiter, Venus (and Waxing Moon / Mercury if well-placed)
Malefics: Saturn, Mars, Rahu, Ketu, Sun (and Waning Moon / Mercury if poorly placed)

Conditional Planets:
  • Mercury: Benefic when alone/with benefics; Malefic when with malefics.
  • Moon: Benefic when waxing (moving to full); Malefic when waning (moving to new).

column1: What are the key features of the South Indian vs. North Indian charts?
column2:
• South Indian: Signs are fixed, houses change based on Ascendant. Read clockwise. 1st House is indicated by a diagonal line/ASC.
  • North Indian: Houses are fixed (1st House is always top middle diamond), signs change. Read counterclockwise.

column1: How do the Planets and Signs correspond to the 7 Chakras?
column2:
• 1st (Root): Saturn (Capricorn/Aquarius)
  • 2nd (Sacral): Jupiter (Sagittarius/Pisces)
  • 3rd (Solar Plexus): Mars (Aries/Scorpio)
  • 4th (Heart): Venus (Taurus/Libra)
  • 5th (Throat): Mercury (Gemini/Virgo)
  • 6th (Third Eye): Sun (Leo - Right side) & Moon (Cancer - Left side)
  • 7th (Crown): None (beyond karma and planetary influence)

column1: What are the planetary Rulerships of the 12 Zodiac signs?
column2:
• Sun: Leo
  • Moon: Cancer
  • Mercury: Gemini & Virgo
  • Venus: Taurus & Libra
  • Mars: Aries & Scorpio
  • Jupiter: Sagittarius & Pisces
  • Saturn: Capricorn & Aquarius
  • Rahu & Ketu: Act like the lord of the sign they are placed in.

column1: What are the Genders of the planets, and under what 3 conditions are they strongest?
column2:
• Masculine: Sun, Mars, Jupiter. (Strongest in: Odd/Active signs, during the daytime, and waxing moon).
  • Feminine: Moon, Venus. (Strongest in: Even/Passive signs, at night, and waning moon).
  • Neutral: Mercury, Saturn.

column1: Which planets gain Digbala (directional strength) in the 10th house (South), and why?
column2:
Sun and Mars.
Why: The Sun (King) and Mars (General) thrive where they can take action and be in charge.

column1: Which planets gain Digbala (directional strength) in the 4th house (North), and why?
column2:
Moon and Venus.
Why: They are nurturers and function best in the house of home, inner consciousness, and comfort.

column1: Which planets gain Digbala (directional strength) in the 7th house (West), and why?
column2:
Saturn.
Why: Saturn represents sorrow and delays. The 7th house is the furthest away from the Ascendant (the physical body).

column1: Which planets gain Digbala (directional strength) in the 1st house (East), and why?
column2:
Mercury and Jupiter.
Why: They promote well-being, self-promotion, and life management, which align best with the Ascendant.

column1: What does the Ascendant (Lagna) represent as a foundation of the chart?
column2: The physical form (the vessel / physical body). It is our entry point into the world, and it sets the foundation for how all planets function and what areas of life they rule.

column1: What does the Moon (Chandra Lagna) represent as a foundation of the chart?
column2: The astral body (emotions, memories, energetic flows), the embodied soul / personality, history of past lives, and what we are comfortable with.

column1: What does the Sun (Surya Lagna) represent as a foundation of the chart?
column2: The causal body, the absolute Spirit / pure Consciousness, and the initial impulse of the Soul (Divine spark) before embodiment.
